correctness.rationale: A connected cactus incidence map splits as an invertible image of a direct sum of zero-sum cycle spaces and bridge lines. The polar of its abstract free sum is a product of cube sections and intervals. Vertices of each cycle cube section have constant squared norm equal to the cycle length for even cycles and length minus one for odd cycles. Invariant block scalar John shapes thus obey a single linear containment constraint; strictly concave log determinant gives the stated coefficients. The Löwner condition on all signed incidence generators gives independent exact lower bounds attained at equality. The transformed covariance sums, volume determinants, tangent facets, tangent vertices and homothety criterion follow without asymptotic or enumeration assumptions. Verified 61 concrete cactus examples, 26,006 exact facet contacts, 998 signed generator contacts using included Python 3 rational checker; those tests are consistency evidence only.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete exact classification of the two canonical maximal-volume inscribed and minimal-volume enclosing ellipsoids for all connected cactus symmetric edge polytopes. Their Laplacian weights detect odd/even cycles and bridges; every facet and vertex has a certified contact role. The strict homothety criterion distinguishes cacti with the same combinatorial dimension but differing block parity/length, and the weighted spanning-tree product yields exact Euclidean volumes. This is structurally stronger than either graph facet enumeration or a single-cycle inradius computation.
